info.title: ChatVia.ai API
info.description:
Every request carries your bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

## Pagination

Every list endpoint returns one page of items, newest first:

```json
{
  "data": ["…"],
  "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6MTg2LCJfcG9pbnRzVG9OZXh0SXRlbXMiOnRydWV9"
}
```

To get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response back as the
`cursor` query parameter. Leave `cursor` out for the first page. On the
last page `next_cursor` is `null`: stop there.

`per_page` sets how many items a page holds, from 1 to 100 (25 when left
out). A value outside that range is brought into range, not rejected.

A cursor marks a fixed place in the list, not a page number. Pages stay
stable — items created or deleted while you page through never shift
what you get — and a late page costs the server no more than the first.
That is also why there are no page numbers and no total count.

Treat the cursor as an opaque string: send back exactly the
`next_cursor` you received, and never build or edit one. A cursor the
endpoint did not hand out starts the list again at the first page.

## Chatting with an agent

Open a conversation with `POST /v1/agents/{id}/conversations`, then
send each message with `POST …/conversations/{id}/messages`. By
default the reply comes back as one JSON response once it is
finished. Add `stream: true` to the body (or send an
`Accept: text/event-stream` header) to receive it as server-sent
events instead.

Send a `request_id` of your own with each message to make it safe
to retry: resending the same value within a few minutes replays the
finished reply instead of generating — and counting — a new one.

Tool calls that need a person's approval are not available over the
API; the agent simply does not see those tools.

## Streaming

With streaming on, the response is a `text/event-stream`. Each
frame is one `data:` line of JSON:

```
data: {"v":1,"seq":3,"id":"<message id>","type":"delta","data":{"text":"Hel"}}
```

`seq` counts up from 0 and `id` is the reply message's id. `type`
tells you what `data` holds:

| type | data | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `user_message_id`, `request_id`, `replayed` | the turn began |
| `delta` | `text` | the next piece of the reply — append it |
| `replace` | `text` | a safety check rewrote the reply — replace everything received so far |
| `sources` | `sources` | the knowledge sources the reply cited |
| `tool` | `phase`, `name`, … | the agent is using a tool |
| `meta` | `key`, `value` | extra signals, such as a handoff to a human |
| `error` | `code`, `message`, `retryable` | the turn failed — see the codes below |
| `done` | `reason`, `response_time_ms` | the last frame; `reason` is `complete` or `error` |

The error codes, in both modes: `message_limit_reached` and
`chatter_message_limit_reached` (the monthly cap), `rate_limited`
(try again in a minute), `upstream_unavailable` (the AI provider;
retry), `access_blocked`, and `internal`. The JSON mode answers an
error that happened before any text with the matching HTTP status
(403, 429, 502 or 500); a turn that failed after text began is a
200 with `done_reason: "error"` and the partial text, which is
already stored — retry with a new message, not a repeat.

get.description:
Returns the agents you can access, newest first: an owner sees every
agent; a teammate sees their current team's granted agents. Pass
`?team_id=` to list only one team's agents. The list is paged with a
cursor: to get
the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response as `cursor`. On
the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many agents to return (1 to 100).

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Only list the agents of this team (its id).

get.description:
The workspace's reusable prompts, newest first. Pass a prompt's `id` as
`prompt_id` when creating or updating an agent. The list is paged with
a cursor: to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response
as `cursor`. On the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

delete.description:
The agent is gone at once: its chat address, custom domain and API
routes stop working right away. Its conversations, the knowledge
sources no other agent uses and its uploaded files are then removed in
the background. Account-level MCP servers and functions stay; only
their link to this agent is removed.

get.description:
The workspace's staff accounts, newest first. The list is paged with a
cursor: to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response as
`cursor`. On the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

get.description:
Returns the teams you own, newest first, each with its agents and roles
nested. The list is paged with a cursor: to get the next page, send the
`next_cursor` of the response as `cursor`. On the last page
`next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

get.description: The team with its agents and roles nested.

delete.description:
Deletes the team. Your primary team, your only team, and a team that
still has agents cannot be deleted (422).

Detaches the user from the team; their account is kept. The team owner
cannot be removed.

patch.description:
Updates the role's name, agent access and permissions. A field left out
keeps its current value.

delete.description:
Deletes the role. A role that members still hold cannot be deleted
(422) — move them to another role first.

post.description: Body: `{ user_id: string }` — a user's `id` from `GET /api/v1/users`.
post.summary: Assign a teammate to a role

The MCP servers connected to your account, newest first. The list is
paged with a cursor: to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

post.description:
Adds a custom MCP server by URL (bearer token or no auth; OAuth servers
are connected in the dashboard) and syncs its tool catalog. A server
that cannot be reached or synced is not kept (422).

delete.description:
Deletes a custom MCP server and removes it from every agent it's
attached to. Catalog connectors are disconnected in the dashboard (404
here).

Minimum length 500 characters. Stored in object storage; the path is

post.description:
Opens a conversation with the agent, ready for `POST …/messages`. It
stays hidden from the conversation list until the agent's first reply,
and expires after a day when it never gets one. Pass `chatter_id` to
attribute the conversation to one of your chatters.

get.description:
The conversation with its first 500 messages, oldest first. For longer
conversations, page through `GET …/conversations/{id}/messages`.

The conversation's messages, newest first. The list is paged with a
cursor: to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response as
`cursor`. On the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

post.description:
Sends a message to the agent and answers with its reply. By default the
reply comes back as one JSON response once it is finished. Send
`stream: true` (or an `Accept: text/event-stream` header) to receive it
as server-sent events instead — see the Streaming section above for the
event format. Tool calls that need a person's approval are not available
over the API; such tools are skipped.

Resending the same `request_id` within a few minutes replays the
finished reply instead of generating (and counting) a new one.

200.description: With `stream: true` or `Accept: text/event-stream`: the reply as server-sent events.

get.description:
Your chatters, newest first. The list is paged with a cursor: to get

the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

post.description:
Provisions an end-user (chatter) under your account, granted access to
the agents named by `agent_ids`. Returns the chatter's `id` — pass it
when minting a sign-in link.
Mint a sign-in link for one of your end-users (chatters) into one of your agents.

patch.description:
Updates the chatter's access controls: the monthly message cap and the
deactivation switch. A field left out keeps its current value.

delete.description:
Permanently delete the chatter identified by `chatter` (its `id` from
`POST /api/v1/chatters`) and everything tied to them. This cannot be
undone.

post.description:
Grants the chatter access to the agents named by `agent_ids`. Granting
is idempotent — an agent the chatter already has is simply kept.

delete.description:
Remove the chatter's access to the agents named by `agent_ids`. The
chatter keeps access to any agent not listed. Revoking is idempotent — an
agent the chatter wasn't granted is simply ignored.

get.description:
The agent's inline forms, newest first, each with its submission count.
The list is paged with a cursor: to get the next page, send the
`next_cursor` of the response as `cursor`. On the last page
`next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

post.description:
Defines a new inline form and switches the agent's Forms capability on,
so the agent can start offering it in chat.

patch.description:
A field left out keeps its current value; `schema` is replaced whole
when sent. The slug never changes, so rendered forms keep resolving.

delete.description:
Deletes the form and its submissions. Removing the agent's last form
turns its Forms capability back off.

get.description:
The form's submitted entries, newest first. Pending rows (forms the
agent rendered but the visitor never sent) are left out. The list is
paged with a cursor: to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of
the response as `cursor`. On the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

get.description:
A CSV with one column per form field plus the submitted-at timestamp —
the whole form, or only the submissions named by `ids`. The response is
`text/csv`, not JSON.

The agent's eval runs, newest first. The list is paged with a cursor:
to get the next page, send the `next_cursor` of the response as
`cursor`. On the last page `next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

post.description:
Starts a run over the agent's active eval cases. The cases are scored
asynchronously: the response is the new run with status `running` (or
`completed` right away when the agent has no active cases) — poll
`GET …/evals/runs/{id}` until `finished_at` is set. Every scored case
counts as one message against the workspace's monthly limit.

get.description:
The run's status and counts, with every per-case result scored so far
(oldest first).

The agent's topics, newest first — or, with `scope=available`, every
topic the workspace may attach (its own and the built-in system
topics). The list is paged with a cursor: to get the next page, send
the `next_cursor` of the response as `cursor`. On the last page
`next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `agent` (default) lists the topics attached to the agent; `available` lists every topic the workspace may attach (its own and the built-in system topics).

post.description:
Attaches an existing topic by `topic_id` (a system topic or one of the
workspace's own), or creates a new workspace topic from `topic` +
`description` and attaches it.

patch.description:
Renames / re-describes one of the workspace's own topics. System topics
are read-only and answer 403.

delete.description:
Detaches the topic from the agent. A workspace topic no agent uses any
more is deleted; system topics stay for other agents.

get.description:
Headline numbers (messages, conversations, response times, feedback),
the per-day series for the selected range, activity patterns, visitor
countries and the most used knowledge files.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: First day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to 6 days ago.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to today.

get.description:
Visitor-message sentiment per day and summed over the range. Row keys
are the sentiment values (`positive`, `neutral`, `negative`) plus
`unspecified` for messages that were never analysed.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: First day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to 6 days ago.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to today.

get.description:
Visitor-message tone per day and summed over the range. Row keys are
the tone values plus `unspecified` for messages that were never
analysed.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: First day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to 6 days ago.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to today.

get.description:
Each busy topic's conversation counts per day over the range, the
totals per topic and the overall total.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: First day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to 6 days ago.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last day of the range (`Y-m-d`). Defaults to today.

get.description:
The knowledge sources, webhook functions and MCP tools the agent used
most, all time, with their last use. Labels are recorded at call time,
so a deleted source keeps its real name.

Every tool call any of the workspace's agents made — one immutable row

and `connector`. The list is paged with a cursor: to get the next page,
send the `next_cursor` of the response as `cursor`. On the last page
`next_cursor` is null.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many items to return (1 to 100).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Only calls with this gateway outcome: `auto`, `approved`, `denied`, `rate_limited` or `not_offered`.

parameters.name: connector
parameters.description: Only calls of this catalog connector (its slug).

AssignRoleMemberRequest.description:
Public-API body for putting a user on a team role. Same gate as the web
side (TeamPolicy::updateTeamMember). `user_id` is the user's public id and
must name a teammate of the caller's own workspace — any other value is a
validation error, never a lookup, so the endpoint cannot confirm another
workspace's ids and a malformed id never reaches the uuid column.

user_id.description: ID of the teammate to put on the role (see `GET /api/v1/users`).

AssignRoleMemberRequest.title: AssignRoleMemberRequest

AttachAgentFunctionRequest.description:
Attach one of your workspace's functions to an agent, named by the
function's `id`. An id that is not one of your functions fails validation.

function_id.description: ID of the function to attach.

AttachAgentFunctionRequest.title: AttachAgentFunctionRequest

AttachAgentMcpRequest.description:
Attach one of your workspace's MCP servers to an agent, named by the
server's `id`. An id that is not one of your servers fails validation.

mcp_id.description: ID of the MCP server to attach.

AttachAgentMcpRequest.title: AttachAgentMcpRequest

CrawlSourceUrlRequest.description:
Validates a website added as a knowledge source through the public API.
Access to the agent is checked by the route middleware.

url.description: The website address to crawl and train on.

include_paths.description:
Path globs to keep, comma-separated (e.g. `/docs,/help`).
Empty means the whole site.

CrawlSourceUrlRequest.title: CrawlSourceUrlRequest

FormType.description: What a form collects. The type does not change how a submission is stored or delivered; it labels the form for the owner and in the CRM payload (`form_type`).
FormType.title: FormType

FunctionAuthType.description: How ChatVia.ai authenticates a function's outbound webhook call.
FunctionAuthType.title: FunctionAuthType

FunctionWebhookMethod.description: HTTP method ChatVia.ai uses when calling a function's webhook. The values are stored in `functions.webhook_method` and shown in the public API.
FunctionWebhookMethod.title: FunctionWebhookMethod

GrantApiChatterAgentsRequest.description:
The agents to grant a chatter. Every agent id must be one of your agents:
any other id fails validation, and no access is granted.

agent_ids.description:
IDs of the agents to grant the chatter access to. Grants the
chatter already holds are kept as they are.

GrantApiChatterAgentsRequest.title: GrantApiChatterAgentsRequest

SaveApiTeamRoleRequest.description:
A team role's name, agent access and permissions. Only the workspace owner
may change a team's roles. An agent id that is not one of the team's agents
fails validation.

all_agents.description: Grant access to every agent in the team.

agent_ids.description: IDs of the agents this role can access (ignored when all_agents is true).

permissions.description: Permission codes to grant the role's members.

SaveApiTeamRoleRequest.title: SaveApiTeamRoleRequest

SendApiMessageRequest.description:
A message sent to an agent over the public API. Carries no `toData()`:
the stream DTO is built by StreamRequestDataFactory::forApi(), the one
sanctioned Request-to-domain bridge, so the mapping exists only once.

message.description: The message text to send to the agent.

stream.description:
`true` streams the reply as server-sent events. Sending an
`Accept: text/event-stream` header does the same.

request_id.description:
Your idempotency key. Resending the same value replays the
finished reply instead of generating (and counting) a new one.

SendApiMessageRequest.title: SendApiMessageRequest

StoreApiAgentRequest.description:
Public API: validates creating an agent in one of the workspace's teams.
Takes a name, the team id, whether the agent is public, and either system
instructions or a saved prompt id.

name.description: Display name for the agent, shown in the dashboard and chat header.

team_id.description: The id of the team this agent belongs to.

system_instructions.description: System prompt that defines the agent's behaviour, tone, and rules. Cannot be combined with prompt_id.

prompt_id.description: The id of a reusable saved prompt to use instead of system_instructions. Cannot be combined with system_instructions.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key/value pairs to attach to the agent — for example your own reference ids.

is_public.description: Whether the agent's chat is publicly reachable without a sign-in link.

StoreApiAgentRequest.title: StoreApiAgentRequest

StoreApiChatterRequest.description:
A new chatter and the agents they may use. Every agent id must be one of
your agents: any other id fails validation, and no chatter is created.

agent_ids.description: IDs of the agents the chatter may sign in to. Provide at least one.

email.description:
The chatter's login email. Unique among your chatters only
(checked when the chatter is created), so the answer never
tells whether an email is used anywhere else.

password.description: The chatter's password. At least 8 characters.

StoreApiChatterRequest.title: StoreApiChatterRequest

StoreApiConversationRequest.description:
Opening a conversation over the public API: an optional title and an
optional chatter of your workspace the conversation is attributed to.

title.description: A title for the conversation. Defaults to "New Chat".

chatter_id.description:
ID of one of your chatters to attribute the conversation to. The
chatter's monthly message limit then applies to its replies.

StoreApiConversationRequest.title: StoreApiConversationRequest

StoreApiFormRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/agents/{agent}/forms` — define a new inline form: its texts,
type and the field schema the chat renders (at most 30 fields). The same
rules as the dashboard's form builder.

name.description: The form's title, shown above the rendered form.

subtitle.description: Visitor-facing blurb shown under the title.

success_message.description: Shown to the visitor after a successful submission.

agent_instructions.description: Guidance for the agent on when to offer this form.

is_active.description: Whether the agent may render the form. Defaults to true.

schema.description: The field definitions the chat renders, in order (1–30 fields).

lead_field_map.description: Maps field keys to the standard lead fields.

StoreApiFormRequest.title: StoreApiFormRequest

StoreApiFunctionRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/functions` — define a new webhook function. Credentials
arrive flat (`auth_value`, `auth_header_name`) and are stored encrypted.

internal_name.description:
The name the model calls the function by: letters, digits and
underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. `get_order_status`).

display_name.description: A human-friendly name shown in the dashboard and chat activity.

description.description: What the function does and when to call it — written for the model.

parameters_schema.description: A JSON Schema object describing the function's arguments.

webhook_url.description: The HTTPS endpoint the function call is sent to.

webhook_method.description: The HTTP method of the webhook call. Defaults to POST.

webhook_headers.description: Extra headers to send with every webhook call, as `{name: value}`.

auth_type.description: How the webhook call authenticates: `none`, `bearer`, `header` or `hmac`.

auth_header_name.description: The header the secret is sent in, with the `header` auth type.

auth_value.description:
The secret: the bearer token, header value or HMAC key. Stored
encrypted and never returned.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the webhook, in milliseconds (1000–30000).

is_enabled.description: Whether agents may call the function.

StoreApiFunctionRequest.title: StoreApiFunctionRequest

StoreApiMcpServerRequest.description:
A custom MCP server added over the public API: a name, the endpoint URL
and a bearer token or no auth. OAuth servers need a browser redirect, so
they are connected in the dashboard instead.

auth_strategy.description:
How calls to the server authenticate: `token` sends the bearer
token below; `none` sends nothing. OAuth servers are connected
in the dashboard.

token.description:
The bearer token, required with the `token` strategy. Stored
encrypted and never returned.

StoreApiMcpServerRequest.title: StoreApiMcpServerRequest

StoreApiTeamRequest.description: A new team's name. Only the workspace owner may create teams.
StoreApiTeamRequest.title: StoreApiTeamRequest

StoreApiTopicRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/agents/{agent}/topics` — give the agent a topic: either
attach an existing one by `topic_id` (a system topic or one of the
workspace's own), or create a new workspace topic from `topic` +
`description`.

topic_id.description: The ID of an existing topic to attach. Leave it out to create one.

description.description: What conversations the topic covers — written for the analysis model.

StoreApiTopicRequest.title: StoreApiTopicRequest

StoreChatterSignInLinkRequest.description:
The agent and the person a sign-in link is for. Both must be in your
workspace: any other id is a validation error (422), worded the same for
"unknown" and "someone else's", so the answer never shows whether an id
exists somewhere else.

agent_id.description: ID of the agent to sign the user into.

user_id.description:
ID of the user the link signs in: one of your chatters, or the
owner or a teammate of your workspace (see `GET /api/v1/users`).

ttl_seconds.description: How long the link stays valid, in seconds (60–86400). Defaults to one hour.

StoreChatterSignInLinkRequest.title: StoreChatterSignInLinkRequest

StoreSourceQaRequest.description:
A curated question-and-answer entry added over the public API. Unlike the
dashboard's form, `questions` is a plain array of strings.

title.description: A short name for the entry, shown in the dashboard's Q&A list.

questions.description: The phrasings of the question, one string each.

answer.description:
The answer the agent gives word for word when a visitor asks
one of the questions.

StoreSourceQaRequest.title: StoreSourceQaRequest

StoreSourceTextRequest.description:
Validates a text added as a knowledge source through the public API. Access
to the agent is checked by the route middleware.

content.description: The text to train on, at least 500 characters.

StoreSourceTextRequest.title: StoreSourceTextRequest

ToolCallOutcome.description: How one tool call was resolved, as recorded in the governance audit: - Auto        → ran without a human in the loop.   - Approved    → was gated, and a person approved it before it ran.   - Denied      → was gated, and a person declined it, so it never ran.   - RateLimited → was blocked by the per-tool rate limit, so it never ran.   - NotOffered  → named a tool the agent was not offered on that turn (an                   invented or stale name), so it never ran.  The values are stored in `agent_activity` rows (a Postgres CHECK lists them, so a new case needs a migration) and filtered on in the audit screens, so they must not change.
ToolCallOutcome.title: ToolCallOutcome

UpdateApiAgentRequest.description:
Public API: validates a partial update of an agent. Only the fields sent are
changed; system instructions and a saved prompt id cannot be sent together.
Agent access and the `agent.setup` permission are checked by the route
middleware.

name.description: Display name for the agent, shown in the dashboard and chat header.

system_instructions.description: System prompt that defines the agent's behaviour, tone, and rules. Cannot be combined with prompt_id.

prompt_id.description: The id of a reusable saved prompt to use instead of system_instructions. Cannot be combined with system_instructions.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key/value pairs to attach to the agent — for example your own reference ids.

is_public.description: Whether the agent's chat is publicly reachable without a sign-in link.

UpdateApiAgentRequest.title: UpdateApiAgentRequest

UpdateApiChatterRequest.description:
Updating a chatter's access controls over the public API: the monthly
message cap and the deactivation switch. A field left out keeps its
current value.

messages_limit.description: The chatter's monthly message cap. Null removes the limit.

deactivated.description:
`true` switches the account off: the chatter can no longer sign
in or send messages. `false` switches it back on.

deactivation_reason.description: Shown nowhere publicly; kept for your own records.

UpdateApiChatterRequest.title: UpdateApiChatterRequest

UpdateApiFormRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/agents/{agent}/forms/{form}` — change an inline form. A
field left out keeps its current value; `schema` is replaced whole when
sent.

name.description: The form's title, shown above the rendered form.

subtitle.description: Visitor-facing blurb shown under the title.

success_message.description: Shown to the visitor after a successful submission.

agent_instructions.description: Guidance for the agent on when to offer this form.

is_active.description: Whether the agent may render the form.

schema.description: The full replacement field list, in order (1–30 fields).

lead_field_map.description: Maps field keys to the standard lead fields. Null clears the map.

UpdateApiFormRequest.title: UpdateApiFormRequest

UpdateApiFunctionRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/functions/{function}` — change only the fields sent. When
`auth_type` is sent, the matching credential must be sent with it.

internal_name.description:
The name the model calls the function by: letters, digits and
underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. `get_order_status`).

display_name.description: A human-friendly name shown in the dashboard and chat activity.

description.description: What the function does and when to call it — written for the model.

parameters_schema.description: A JSON Schema object describing the function's arguments.

webhook_url.description: The HTTPS endpoint the function call is sent to.

webhook_method.description: The HTTP method of the webhook call.

webhook_headers.description: Extra headers to send with every webhook call, as `{name: value}`.

auth_type.description: How the webhook call authenticates: `none`, `bearer`, `header` or `hmac`.

auth_header_name.description: The header the secret is sent in, with the `header` auth type.

auth_value.description:
The secret: the bearer token, header value or HMAC key. Stored
encrypted and never returned.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the webhook, in milliseconds (1000–30000).

is_enabled.description: Whether agents may call the function.

UpdateApiFunctionRequest.title: UpdateApiFunctionRequest

UpdateApiTeamRequest.description: A team's new name. Only the workspace owner may rename a team.
UpdateApiTeamRequest.title: UpdateApiTeamRequest

UpdateApiTeamRoleRequest.description:
A partial update of a team role: a field left out keeps its current value
(the store request, SaveApiTeamRoleRequest, requires the full shape). Only
the workspace owner may change a team's roles.

all_agents.description: Grant access to every agent in the team.

agent_ids.description: IDs of the agents this role can access (ignored when all_agents is true).

permissions.description: Permission codes to grant the role's members.

UpdateApiTeamRoleRequest.title: UpdateApiTeamRoleRequest

UpdateApiTopicRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/agents/{agent}/topics/{topic}` — rename / re-describe one of
the workspace's own topics (system topics are read-only).

description.description: What conversations the topic covers — written for the analysis model.

UpdateApiTopicRequest.title: UpdateApiTopicRequest

UploadSourceFileRequest.description:
Validates a knowledge-file upload through the public API. Access to the
agent is checked by the route middleware.

file.description:
The document to train on, as a multipart upload. Accepted
formats and the size cap match the dashboard's uploader; a
password-protected PDF is rejected.

UploadSourceFileRequest.title: UploadSourceFileRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
